title: SidebarNav
wrapsNative: Buttons with Label-style rows on the canvas, a DisclosureGroup-style row with a chevron, MonarchBadge counts and MonarchDivider; NavigationSplitView with List(selection:) and listStyle(.sidebar) remains the choice when the app wants system sidebar behaviour
summary: The standard sidebar: a List with the sidebar style in the first column of a NavigationSplitView, with sections, nested groups, counts and the current page. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For the navigation of an app with many destinations, or sections that group them, on an iPad. On a phone the same code becomes a list that pushes the selected screen.
whenNotToUse: For three to five destinations on a phone use TabView (see bottom-tab-bar). For choosing among views of one screen use MonarchTabs.
api: DisclosureGroup(isExpanded: Binding<Bool>, content: () -> Content, label: () -> Label)
func listStyle(_ style: some ListStyle) -> some View
func badge(_ count: Int) -> some View

states.name: current page
states.description: The selected row has the system's selection background.

states.name: group open or closed
states.description: A DisclosureGroup shows or hides its rows, with a chevron that turns.

states.name: sidebar hidden
states.description: On an iPad the person can hide the sidebar with the system's toolbar button or a swipe; columnVisibility reads and sets it.

states.name: compact width
states.description: The sidebar is the first screen of a stack and a row pushes its destination.

appearance: The system draws the sidebar, its material, the section headers, the selection and the counts set with badge. Row icons take the tint, which monarchTheme sets to the theme's accent.
platformNotes: The web SidebarNav renders sections of links with nested groups, count badges with a tone, a current page from the path, an icon-only collapsed mode with tooltips, and a header and footer. On iOS rows are selections, not links, and the current page is the List's selection. The collapsed icon-only rail does not exist on iOS; the sidebar is shown or hidden as a whole. badgeTone has no equivalent: the system badge is one colour. The header and footer are safeAreaInset on the List or toolbar items. Android uses a navigation drawer or rail.
accessibility: System behaviour: section titles are headings, and the selected row is read as selected.
System behaviour: a DisclosureGroup is read as collapsed or expanded and toggles with a double tap.
System behaviour: a badge is read after the row's title.
System behaviour: with a hardware keyboard the arrow keys move the selection and open and close groups.
Use Label so each row has a title; the icon is decorative.
edgeCases: The selection must be optional: at a compact width nothing is selected until a row is tapped.
A DisclosureGroup's own label is not selectable unless it has a tag.
Section headers in a sidebar are styled by the system; do not restyle them per app.

examples.title: Sections, nested groups and badges
examples.template:
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: theme.spacing.space1) {
    row({{main.0.label}}, systemImage: "house", tag: "home")
    row({{main.1.label}}, systemImage: "tray", tag: "inbox", badge: {{main.1.badge}})
    row({{main.2.label}}, systemImage: "calendar", tag: "calendar")
    sectionLabel({{teamsLabel}})
    group({{teams.0.label}}, isOpen: $isDesignOpen, items: [({{teams.0.items.0.label}}, {{teams.0.items.0.badge}}, {{teams.0.items.0.badgeTone|tone}}), ({{teams.0.items.1.label}}, {{teams.0.items.1.badge}}, {{teams.0.items.1.badgeTone|tone}})], tag: "design")
    group({{teams.1.label}}, isOpen: $isResearchOpen, items: [({{teams.1.items.0.label}}, nil, .neutral), ({{teams.1.items.1.label}}, nil, .neutral)], tag: "research")
    sectionLabel({{workspaceLabel}})
    row({{settings.label}}, systemImage: "gearshape", tag: "settings")
    MonarchDivider().padding(.top, theme.spacing.space8)
    Button {} label: {
        HStack(spacing: theme.spacing.space2) {
            Image(systemName: "sidebar.left").frame(width: 20)
            Text("Collapse sidebar")
        }
        .monarchTextStyle(.label)
        .foregroundStyle(theme.colors.textMuted)
        .padding(.horizontal, theme.spacing.space2)
        .frame(minHeight: 44)
    }
    .buttonStyle(.plain)
}
.padding(.horizontal)
examples.code:
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: theme.spacing.space1) {
    row("Home", systemImage: "house", tag: "home")
    row("Inbox", systemImage: "tray", tag: "inbox", badge: 4)

    sectionLabel("Teams")
    group("Design", isOpen: $isDesignOpen, items: [("Issues", 12, .neutral), ("Backlog", 48, .neutral)], tag: "design")
    group("Research", isOpen: $isResearchOpen, items: [("Issues", nil, .neutral), ("Notes", nil, .neutral)], tag: "research")
    sectionLabel("Workspace")
    row("Settings", systemImage: "gearshape", tag: "settings")
    MonarchDivider().padding(.top, theme.spacing.space8)
    Button {} label: {
        HStack(spacing: theme.spacing.space2) {
            Image(systemName: "sidebar.left").frame(width: 20)
            Text("Collapse sidebar")
        }
        .monarchTextStyle(.label)
        .foregroundStyle(theme.colors.textMuted)
        .padding(.horizontal, theme.spacing.space2)
        .frame(minHeight: 44)
    }
    .buttonStyle(.plain)
}
.padding(.horizontal)
